 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE HARISH KUMAR  ORAL JUDGMENT  Date : 12-09-2024  Heard the parties.

2. The petitioner is aggrieved by the order dated  27.02.2023 , passed by the Presiding Officer, Land Acquisition and Resettlement Authority, Bhagalpur by which the respondent no. 7 has directed the petitioner to withdraw the petition filed in compliance with the order dated 16.11.2022 passed in CWJC No. 3406 of 2022 and directed to file the case before the competent authority without deciding the matter on merit.

entities.text: Land Acquisition and Resettlement Authority, Bhagalpur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Learned Advocate for the petitioner further seeks a direction to make payment of half amount of the award prepared in Award Nos. 67,
68 and 70 on the basis of Land Acquisition Case No. 17 of 2019-20 by the District Land Acquisition Officer, Bhagalpur for construction of National Highway No. 80 (Munger Mirzachouki four lane).
3.

Learned Advocate for the petitioner contended that Patna High Court CWJC No.13633 of 2024 dt.12-09-2024 the land, in question, the description of which has been duly mentioned in paragraph no. 9 are recorded in the name of petitioner's father and the legal heirs of Kallar Choudhary.
However, the land was acquired for construction of National Highway No. 80.

For the said purpose,
a notification was duly published in the official gazette.

In pursuant thereto, Land Acquisition Case No. 17 of 2019-20 was initiated and after determination of compensation amount, the land holders were directed to appear before the District Land Acquisition Officer, Bhagalpur on 05.09.2021 to receive the calculated and fixed amount of compensation.

The petitioner being dissatisfied with the aforesaid award filed petition before the District Land Acquisition Officer, Bhagalpur claiming half of the share in the acquired land, but the same has not been considered.

sentences.text: The petitioner had earlier approached before this Court in CWJC No. 3406 of 2022, for ventilating his grievance, the writ petition was disposed off with a direction to approach LAARA; but their claims were not entertained by LAARA, on being found no jurisdiction.

5. At this juncture, learned Advocate for the State submits at the bar that if the petitioner has any grievance with regard to the apportionment of the award, the petitioner has Patna High Court CWJC No.13633 of 2024 dt.12-09-2024 remedy available before the Commissioner-cum-Arbitrator, duly appointed under the notification of the Government of India.

6. In view of the nature of the grievance, this Court deems it proper to dispose of the writ petition w i t h a l i b e r t y t o t h e p e t i t i o n e r t o a p p r o a c h b e f o r e t h e d u l y a p p o i n t e d Commissioner-cum-Arbitrator, Bhagalpur under Section 3 (G) 5 of the National Highways Act, 1956 preferably within a period of four weeks, from today.

7 . I f t h e p e t i t i o n e r f i l e s a p p r o p r i a t e a p p l i c a t i o n b e f o r e t h e a f o r e n o t e d Commissioner-cum-Arbitrator, Bhagalpur, the same shall be disposed off expeditiously in accordance with law, preferably within a period of three months after giving opportunity to all the stakeholders.

(Harish Kumar, J) shivank/-
